To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The SIMPLE collaboration has performed a search for dark matter using a 60-gram natural germanium target, and found no evidence for dark matter interactions.

(i) the SIMPLE experiment has set the most stringent limits on dark matter spin-independent interactions in the 10 GeV/c2 mass range, (ii) the SIMPLE experiment is the only dark matter experiment with a published limit in the 10 to 100 GeV/c2 range, (iii) the SIMPLE experiment was the first experiment to report a limit on spin-dependent dark matter interactions, (iv) the SIMPLE experiment demonstrated the first direct detection of a dark matter candidate,

1) SIMPLE’s 2008 data are consistent with background-only, with no evidence for dark matter; 2) The SIMPLE collaboration is currently constructing a heavy detector for application in the spin-independent search; and 3) The SIMPLE collaboration will soon begin taking data in a new search for spin-dependent dark matter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
searches for dark matter in the form of weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs), and is based on the use of ultra-low background germanium detectors.
the development, construction and operation of low-background, high-efficiency, low-energy threshold germanium detectors for the direct detection of dark matter.
the search for Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs) in a direct search for the WIMP-nucleus elastic scattering signal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SIMPLE program has not been able to find a signal of dark matter.
the SIMPLE experiment is not yet sensitive to the dark matter signal.
there is still nothing to report.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SIMPLE is SIMPLE, and SIMPLE is good.

SIMPLE has been successful in demonstrating that a low-background search with a low-mass detector can be carried out with a high level of sophistication, and with a high level (in the 10-9 pb-1 region) of sensitivity.
we are still searching, with the hope that we will soon see a signal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of “light” detectors is not a requirement for the SIMPLE experiment.
a SIMPLE detector can provide an order of magnitude improvement in sensitivity for spin-independent dark matter interactions.
SIMPLE has the sensitivity to detect the expected signal for a 1 GeV WIMP.
